newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds close sharply higher.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds closed sharply higher on Thursday amid active trading and strong demand, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.43 pct to 100.43
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.2 pct to 100.20.
Volume was high at 232 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds and Makams.

On Wednesday trading was suspended to enable the exchange to alter the system for pricing bonds, introduce new indices and rewind the rest to 100 points. The change was technical and did not cause a change in the actual value of the bonds.

"The new year opened with extremely strong demand for unlinked bonds and Makams of almost one billion shekels. There is simply no logical explanation for the hysteria," said Baruch Glicksberg of Clal Insurance.
Traders said demand for unlinked bonds reached 390 million shekels against virtually no supply. Demand for Makams totalled a high 575 million shekels.

"Investors believe that the Bank of Israel will lower its short term rate by 1.5 percentage point during the next six months and that yields on unlinked bonds will fall to 4.0 percent by the end of the year," Glicksberg added.

"Israeli companies are converting dollars into shekels and investing the money in unlinked bonds because yields are high and the risk is minimal," said Gidi Halperin, investment manger at Meitav Investments and Securities.
Traders said the big mutual funds, which sold unlinked bonds before the end of the year to gain tax benefits, were buying them back today.
"Linked bonds also rose but on much slower pace. The main gainers were short- and medium-term bonds," Halperin said.

Traders said dollar-linked bonds closed lower following the rise of the shekel against the dollar. On Thursday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2420 shekels against 3.2510 shekels on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
